previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of chronic alcohol use, CAD, CABG, COPD, and esophagitis was admitted for acute abdominal pain, vomiting, and tachypnea. He presented with leukocytosis, lactic acidosis, and an elevated anion gap, raising concern for sepsis or mesenteric ischemia. Imaging ruled out surgical causes but showed esophageal thickening and fatty liver. His symptoms were attributed to alcoholic gastritis and esophagitis. He developed paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, managed initially with metoprolol and then transitioned to diltiazem due to symptomatic bradycardia. Electrolyte abnormalities, including hypomagnesemia and hypophosphatemia, were corrected. Pleural effusions developed, likely related to fluid shifts and atrial fibrillation, and were managed with diuresis. He improved with IV fluids, acid suppression, and alcohol cessation counseling. He was discharged on aspirin, diltiazem ER, and optimized GI medications, with strict instructions to abstain from alcohol and follow up with primary care, cardiology, and gastroenterology.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ with chest pain.

TECHNIQUE:
Frontal and lateral radiographs of the chest were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:
There is faint right basilar opacity likely representing atelectasis,
consolidation from infection or aspiration cannot be excluded in the
appropriate clinical setting.  No pleural effusion, no pneumothorax.
There is a fracture of the upper most sternal wire, unchanged.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ male with left lower quadrant pain and fever. 
Evaluate for diverticulitis.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis were displayed with 5-mm slice thickness with 130 mL Omnipaque
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were displayed with 5-mm
slice thickness.

CT ABDOMEN:  The visualized lung bases demonstrate dependent bibasilar
atelectasis.  There is no pericardial effusion.  Right pleural thickening is
improved from the prior study with interval resolution of the effusion.  There
is no left effusion.  There is a moderate-to-large hiatal hernia.

The liver is normal.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic bile duct dilation. 
Stones within the gallbladder are unchanged, without gallbladder wall edema or
pericholecystic fluid.  The spleen and pancreas are normal.  The bilateral
adrenal glands are normal.  The kidneys enhance symmetrically and excrete
contrast promptly without hydronephrosis.  Bilateral renal cysts are
redemonstrated, unchanged from ___, the largest in the right renal lower
pole measuring 2.6 cm.

Diverticula are seen throughout the large bowel without inflammatory changes. 
The small and large bowel are normal in course and caliber without
obstruction.  The appendix is normal.  There is moderate colonic fecal
loading.  There is no free fluid and no free air.  No pathologically enlarged
mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymph nodes are identified.  Incidentally noted
is a retroaortic left renal vein.  The main portal vein, splenic vein, and SMV
are patent.  Atherosclerotic calcifications are seen throughout the aorta and
iliac arteries with moderate-to-severe narrowing at the origin of the SMA due
to soft plaque, unchanged from and better assessed on ___. Beyond the
stenosis, the SMA is patent. The celiac axis and ___ are patent.

CT PELVIS:  The rectum is normal. Diverticula are seen in the sigmoid colon
without inflammatory changes.  The bladder is normal and the right ureteral
jet is demonstrated.  The prostate is normal.  There is no free fluid and no
pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOWS:  No bone finding suspicious for infection or malignancy is seen.
Degenerative changes predominantly in the lower thoracic spine are similar in
appearance to ___. The patient is status post median sternotomy.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intra-abdominal process. No CT explanation for patient's pain.
2.  Diverticulosis without diverticulitis.
3.  Cholelithiasis without acute cholecystitis.
4.  Moderate-to-severe narrowing of the origin of the SMA, similar in
appearance to ___. Beyond the stenosis, the SMA is patent.

DLP:  505.39 mGy-cm.
